chapters.title: Introduction
chapters.summary: Privacy and data protection: how they differ, why they matter in data sharing, and where GDPR fits in the data ecosystem.
topics: Introduces the concepts of privacy and data protection
Differentiates privacy from data protection
Discusses the importance of privacy in data sharing
Briefly introduces GDPR and its role in the data ecosystem

chapters.title: Foundations of GDPR
chapters.summary: An introduction to GDPR’s legal bases, scope, and applicability, including its impact on data sharing and the data economy.
topics: Provides a foundational understanding of GDPR and its legal bases
Explains the scope and applicability of GDPR
Highlights its impact on data sharing and the economy, including fines and violations

chapters.title: Data Sharing and the Data Economy
chapters.summary: Explore trust, data quality, and interoperability, and the role of data sharing in sectors such as healthcare.
topics: Explores the concepts of data sharing, trust, quality, and interoperability
Introduces the data economy and its relation to sharing practices
Highlights applications in sectors like healthcare

chapters.title: Ethical Considerations in Data Sharing
chapters.summary: Examine data minimization, transparency, and the ethical choices that shape responsible data practices.
topics: Focuses on ethical principles like data minimization and transparency
Discusses what to avoid to prevent unethical data practices

chapters.title: Ensuring GDPR Compliance
chapters.summary: Accountability, compliance strategies, and the technical and organizational measures involved in handling personal data responsibly.
topics: Discusses compliance strategies and the principle of accountability
Provides technical and organizational measures to remain compliant

chapters.title: Building Secure and Interoperable Data Sharing Systems
chapters.summary: Move from principles to system design: data quality, interoperability, trust, decentralized systems, and practical implementation.
topics: Covers data quality, interoperability, and trust from a system design perspective
Introduces decentralized systems (e.g., IPFS)
Shares best practices and common pitfalls

chapters.title: Case Studies
chapters.summary: Explore real-world applications and failure points, including hospital patient monitoring systems.
topics: Analyzes real-world applications and failure points
Includes examples like hospital patient monitoring systems

chapters.title: Trends and Considerations
chapters.summary: A look at global data protection trends and regional regulations, including China’s PIPL and the European AI Act.
topics: Discusses global data protection trends and regional regulations
Examples include China’s PIPL and the European AI Act

chapters.title: Conclusion
chapters.summary: Bring together the key ideas for building secure, ethical, and legally compliant data sharing systems.
topics: Recaps key takeaways from the book

authors.name: Tek Raj Chhetri
bio: Tek Raj Chhetri develops knowledge-centric AI systems for scientific discovery, trustworthy reasoning, and governance-aware deployment. He is a Postdoctoral Associate at MIT and the founder and director of CAIR-Nepal.
His work spans knowledge graphs, foundation models, and privacy-aware data systems, including BrainKB and research on GDPR-compliant data sharing.
topics: Knowledge graphs
Trustworthy AI
Data privacy

authors.name: Semih Yumusak
bio: Semih Yumusak researches large language models, knowledge graphs, and semantic data infrastructure. He is listed as an Assistant Professor in Computer Engineering at TOBB ETÜ.

Previously a Postdoctoral Research Fellow at the University of Southampton, he worked on UPCAST and RAISE. His research includes data-sharing negotiation, ODRL policies, and privacy-aware data marketplaces.
topics: Semantic Web
Data marketplaces
Large language models

authors.name: Luis-Daniel Ibáñez
bio: Luis-Daniel Ibáñez’s research interests include dataset retrieval, Linked Data, and decentralised technologies. He is listed as a Lecturer in Computer Science by the University of Southampton’s Centre for Machine Intelligence.

His work connects data protection and distributed data systems. His published conference biography describes research on blockchain and GDPR, alongside experience coordinating research projects and leading the MSc Data Science programme.
topics: Linked Data
Dataset retrieval
Decentralised systems

authors.name: Anna Fensel
authors.role: Professor of Artificial Intelligence & Data Science
bio: Anna Fensel is a Full Professor in Artificial Intelligence and Data Science at Wageningen University & Research. Her areas of expertise include ontologies, knowledge modelling, Linked Open Data, the Semantic Web, and FAIR data.

She previously held research and academic roles at the University of Innsbruck, Telecommunications Research Center Vienna, and the University of Surrey. She earned her doctorate and habilitation in Computer Science at the University of Innsbruck.
topics: Semantic technologies
Knowledge modelling
FAIR data

authors.name: George Konstantinidis
bio: George Konstantinidis is a Professor at the University of Southampton and a member of the Data, Intelligence and Society research group. His research includes compliant data markets, data integration, and trust in data workflows.
His university profile lists projects including DataPACT and RAISE Suite, alongside work on UPCAST. His publications address policy semantics, consent management, and knowledge graph validation.
topics: Data integration
Policy semantics
Trust & compliance
